key_insight: Embedding random Fourier features into a PINN reduces spectral bias, allowing better capture of sharp elastic-plastic gradients and failure zones in non-associative Mohr-Coulomb geomaterials.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a faster mesh-free surrogate for geotechnical elasto-plastic analysis, potentially reducing FEM cost while preserving physics consistency.
method: Random Fourier feature mapping is added to the PINN input layer to improve high-frequency function representation.
A multi-objective loss enforces equilibrium, constitutive laws, and KKT conditions using FEM supervision.
Strain-adaptive sampling targets localized plastic regions during training.
evidence_signal: Across three benchmark cases, FF-PINN improved most predicted fields, reduced displacement error by up to about 66% and stress error by about 27%, and converged in roughly half the epochs of a standard PINN.
watch_item: Performance depends on high-quality FEM-based training targets and careful tuning of loss weights and sampling near narrow plastic zones.
paper_title: Fourier Feature Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Elasto-Plastic Analysis of Geomaterials with a Non-Associative Mohr-Coulomb Model
